task: Restaurant: replace the end-of-shift result moment (score pill enlargement + label over the live room, then a rival walk to the player and a close-up question) with a dedicated, continuous result stage that turns into the final 'What food do you like?' conversation without returning to gameplay framing.
requirements: SCOPE: only shifts where the rival arrived (rivalArrived() && claimRegistry, same condition that starts the current ceremony) use the new stage. Easy and any shift that ended before the rush keep the existing path unchanged (customer partner, beginTurnaroundApproach, closeup). Do not touch Easy behaviour.

NEW PURE MODULE src/minigames/restaurant/resultStage.js (no three.js, no DOM) with unit tests in resultStage.test.mjs (picked up by npm test like the other *.test.mjs). Export: RESULT_STAGE_TIMING = { reaction: 1.8, labelFade: 0.3, scoreShrink: 0.5, settle: 0.6 } (seconds); RESULT_STAGE_LAYOUT = { player: {x:-1.35,z:-3.75}, rival: {x:1.35,z:-3.75} } (player left, rival right as seen from the camera, which looks toward -z); reactionsFor(outcome) -> {player, rival} where outcome 'player' -> {player:'celebrate', rival:'despair'}, 'rival' -> {player:'dejected', rival:'celebrate'}, 'draw' -> {player:'shrug', rival:'shrug'}; createResultStage({outcome}) returning an object with start() (returns false if already started: the sequence can never trigger twice), advance(dt), and readonly getters active, outcome, phase, elapsed, phaseElapsed, labelVisible, scoreCompact, reactions. Phases in order: 'idle' -> 'reaction' (reaction seconds; labelVisible true) -> 'settling' (labelFade + scoreShrink + settle seconds combined = 1.4 s; labelVisible false from the start of settling; scoreCompact true from the start of settling) -> 'question' (stays until the scene calls markAnswered()) -> 'answered'. advance() returns an array of transition events like [{type:'phase', phase:'settling'}] so the scene reacts once per transition. Unit tests cover: phase order and durations, labelVisible/scoreCompact per phase, reactionsFor for all three outcomes, start() twice returns false, advance before start is a no-op, large dt crossing several phases emits every transition in order, markAnswered only valid in 'question'.

SCENE (src/minigames/restaurant/index.js): replace beginResultCeremony/updateResultCeremony/endResultCeremony and, for the rival path only, beginTurnaroundApproach/updateTurnaroundApproach/beginTurnaround. When updateRoundEnd detects the final resolution on a rival shift: keep the existing delivery feedback (dialogue/notice already in flight may finish, as now), set phase 'result-stage' (a new phase value; the service branch of update() must not run for it, exactly like round-end), create and start the pure stage. The rival walk (TURNAROUND_WALK_*) is NOT used on this path.

FREEZE: from result-stage start through finish, none of these advance: conveyor/belt (updateConveyor and belt slat scroll), customer lifecycle/patience, rival AI (applyRivalEvents / rival.advance / claimRegistry.advance), director, food freshness/carried temperature, player movement/click-to-walk/input actions, service timers. Only the stage clock, character animation, camera, dialogue and the speech prompt advance. Consume/ignore interact presses and canvas clicks during the stage.

STAGING at stage start (one frame, no walk): discard any dish the rival or player carries (discardRivalDish; hide the player's carried dish), hide every customer character and their bubbles/patience strips, hide all dishes still on the belt or on tables, hide the action button, temperature, notices, combo, phase pill, listen-again and the upper-left hint. Place the SAME player and rival objects (no clones, no new characters) at RESULT_STAGE_LAYOUT positions, rotation.y = 0 (faces the camera; Kenney models face +z), position.y = 0. Clear autoTarget and any click-to-walk target.

CAMERA: result composition via cameraRig.setPreset('fixed', ...) with position about [0, 2.55, 2.4] and lookAt about [0, 1.75, -4.6], damping about 3 (a smooth ease from the room view, no hard cut). Both waiters full-body in frame, stopped belt behind them, the MATSUBARA RESTAURANT sign (signAnchor at (0, 2.45, -7.17)) centred between/above them. Conversation framing when 'question' starts: ease slightly closer, e.g. position [0, 2.2, 0.6], lookAt [0, 1.55, -4.2], damping about 3; both waiters still visible, sign still at least partly visible. Tune these numbers by rendering; they are starting values. The camera target object is irrelevant for 'fixed'.

SCORE UI: at stage start the existing score pill (scoreText, text from formatUi(STRINGS.rivalScore, competitionScore.score(claimRegistry.counts)) - the post-rush head-to-head score, NOT solo totals) becomes large at top centre (a new class e.g. restaurant-ui__score--stage, larger than the current --result: roughly 2rem font, top ~1.4rem). The result label (existing .restaurant-ui__result element and existing STRINGS.resultPlayer/resultRival/resultDraw, Japanese, keep them) shows under it. When the pure stage reports labelVisible false the label fades out over RESULT_STAGE_TIMING.labelFade via CSS transition/opacity (then hidden). When scoreCompact becomes true the score smoothly (CSS transition on transform/font-size/top, ~0.5 s) shrinks back to its normal pill size and moves to the top edge (top about .6rem), leaving the centre free. The score never disappears abruptly and stays visible through the question and finish.

REACTIONS (procedural, reaction phase only). The Kenney models are node-animated, not skinned: nodes 'root' > 'leg-left','leg-right','torso' > 'arm-left','arm-right','head' (find with character.getObjectByName; the procedural fallback body uses the same names). Model faces +z; model-left is +x. Pivots: arms at the shoulder, legs at the hip, head at the neck. Rotation conventions: arm-left rotation.z positive swings the arm outward/up (about +2.5 = raised in a V), arm-right uses negative z; rotation.x negative swings a limb forward/up toward the face direction; head.rotation.x negative looks up, positive looks down; torso.rotation.x negative leans back, positive slumps forward. Play the 'static' clip (exists on every model; use playAnimation('static', {fade:0})) during reactions so the mixer holds rest pose, and apply pose rotations AFTER updateAnimation each frame (add a function called after the animation updates at the end of update()). Capture each node's rest rotation first and restore it when the reaction ends. 'celebrate': three energetic hops (character position.y up to ~0.45, ~0.5 s each), both arms raised in a V and pumping (z about +/-2.4 oscillating +/-0.35), a small torso twist, finish on a held victory pose arms high. 'despair' (funny cartoon, never distress): within ~0.25 s drop to the knees - lower the whole character by about 0.45 and swing both legs back (leg rotation.x about +1.35) so they tuck behind; torso upright or leaning back slightly; head looking up (head.rotation.x about -0.45); both arms raised forward-and-up (rotation.x about -2.7, slight outward z) shaking fast and small (about 9 Hz, +/-0.22) as fists shaken at the ceiling. 'dejected' ("aw, I lost", mild): head down (head.rotation.x about +0.4), shoulders/torso slumped forward (torso.rotation.x about +0.18), arms hanging slightly forward and in, a slow small sigh dip in position.y (about -0.04), minimal movement. 'shrug' (draw, friendly, no winner): arms out low with palms-up feel (arm z about +/-0.55, x about -0.5), a quick shoulder lift (torso.position.y +0.04 or small arm bob), head tilt (head.rotation.z about 0.15), then a small nod. Ease in and out of every pose (no snapping). Both characters reach neutral by the end of 'settling'.

SETTLING: when the stage enters 'settling': fade the label, compact the score, ease both characters back to rest pose (restore captured rotations, position.y 0) and switch them to 'idle'; then turn the rival toward the player and the player toward the rival (smoothly over the settle time, rotation.y via atan2 of the relative position, with shortest-angle interpolation). Neither character looks frustrated or celebratory after settling.

QUESTION: when the stage enters 'question': the rival shows dialogue.show({ text: LESSON.question, anchor: rivalCharacter, offsetY: 1.8 }) (the same English turnaround line, 'What food do you like?'), setInstruction(STRINGS.turnaround), beginFocus('restaurant-turnaround'), and promptAnswer(ctx, LESSON, { isActive: () => active, onAccepted: completeTurnaround }) exactly as beginTurnaround does now, so speech recognition, the mic-free fallback, accepted vocabulary and scoring are unchanged. Set turnaroundPartner = { type: 'rival', character: rivalCharacter, customer: null } so completeTurnaround's partner reaction and the debug turnaroundPartner still work. The existing phase value 'turnaround' may be used for the question stage if that keeps promptAnswer/completeTurnaround/finishing untouched - but resultStage.active must stay true until finish, the camera must NOT switch to the old 'closeup' preset, and partner.rotation.y must NOT be reset to 0 on this path (the rival keeps facing the player).

MIC/TALK UI: hud stays hidden during 'reaction' and 'settling' (hud.hide(); syncHud must keep it hidden while the stage is in those phases even if settings changes call setMicFree). It appears only when promptAnswer runs at 'question'. The Japanese rival-challenge reply panel (.restaurant-ui__challenge) must be hidden throughout. Check at 1366x768 and 412x915 that the Talk HUD does not overlap the compact score or the dialogue bubble.

AFTER A CORRECT ANSWER: the rival plays a short friendly positive reaction ('emote-yes'), the player a small one ('emote-yes' too is fine), the existing success SFX ('stamp') plays, then the existing finishing timer calls finish(). Never return to gameplay framing or ROOM_CAMERA.
AUDIO: keep the existing RESULT_STINGS (rising win, falling rival win, two-note draw), triggered by the reaction phase.

DEBUG HOOK (installDebugHook): add resultStage: { active, outcome, phase ('reaction' | 'settling' | 'question' | 'answered' | null when inactive), labelVisible, scoreVisible, scoreCompact, scoreText, playerPosition {x,z}, rivalPosition {x,z}, playerReaction, rivalReaction, conveyorStopped (true when the belt did not advance), cameraPreset, cameraPosition {x,y,z}, signInView (signAnchor projected inside the camera frustum), customersVisible (count of visible customer characters), startCount (number of times the stage started this shift) }. Keep the existing resultCeremony field working (map it onto the new state or remove it only if nothing in scripts/ reads it - grep first) and keep turnaroundPartner.
RESET: enter() and exit() reset all new state (stage object, CSS classes on the score, captured rest rotations, label opacity).
